newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ yields end a touch higher after range trading.
newsitem.headline: NZ yields end a touch higher after range trading.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD (PCT)
90-DAY BILLS (JUN) 92.49 (PREV 92.49) 90-DAYS 7.40 (PREV 7.40)
OVERNIGHT CASH 7.25 PCT (PREV 7.25) US 5-YR 6.77 (PREV 6.76)
* NZ debt ends steady after day of neutral data
* Bonds up a fraction in line with U.S. but still bid
* NZ seen outperforming U.S. on spreads in coming months
New Zealand bonds ended Thursday's session slightly weaker after trading narrow ranges in the face of neutral content in the day's balance of payments and unemployment data.

Statistics New Zealand (SNZ) said the December year current account deficit was NZ$3.9 billion, against a $4.2 billion deficit in the year to September. Economists had picked on average a $4.25 billion deficit.
Treasurer Winston Peters hailed the data as very encouraging, saying the figures suggested the economy was on the right track.

However, one money market dealer said that while the deficit had improved, the lagged impact of the higher New Zealand dollar last year had yet to surface in the trade figures, and people saw the current account deteriorating further over the year.
Meanwhile, the Employment Service said the number of New Zealanders registered as unemployed fell to 152,711 in March from 158,217 in February.

Bankers Trust bond dealer Martin Poulsen said both sets of data had held potential to be bearish for the market, but anecdotal evidence since Tuesday's bullish CPI numbers had supported the idea that the economy was cooling, which had kept an underlying bid tone in the market.
"Overall the market remains bid and I would expect there's a bias to pick up risk on dips," he said.
The money market finished steady, with 90-day bank bills hovering around an unchanged 7.40 percent, which has proved a good support level.
BT's Poulsen said the U.S. Treasury market would inevitably begin to set the stage for local trade as it geared up for a tightening in monetary policy at the Federal Reserve's meeting in May.
However, while New Zealand debt would weaken in sympathy, local short assets were looking strong and BT expected spreads to the U.S. to tend to narrow over the next couple of months.
